To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
N-benzoylated cyanomethyl estes of amino acids have been synthesized and tested for their antitumor, antiinflammatory, and immunosuppressive activities.
N-benzoylated cyanomethyl estes of amino acids possess potent antineoplastic, immunosuppressive, and antiinflammatory activities.

the N-tosy1 and N-Cbz protected L-phenylalanyl cyanomethyl estes were the most active antineoplastic agents in our study, while the N-benzyl and N-carbobenzyloxed L-phenyl-alanyl cyanomethyl derivatives were the best antiinflammatory agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of novel amino acid derivatives with antitumor and anti-inflammatory activities.
the development of a series of N-protecting moieties for the cyanomethyl estesr of amino acids which will enhance the antitumor and anti-inflammatory properties of this class of compounds.
the development of new antineoplastic agents which are active at low doses, and are devoid of significant toxicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the N-protective group is an important structural determinant of the antineoplastic activity of the amino acid cyanomethyl estes, while the antiinflammatory activity is determined by the amino acid side chain.
the N-Cbz-protected cyanomethylesters of the L-amino acids are the most potent antitumor and anti-inflammatory compounds in this series.
the N-benzyl and N-Cbz-protected amino acid cyanomethyl esterase are the most active against both tumor and inflammation in the rodent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-benzyl-protected amino acid analogues are more potent antineoplastics and antiinflammatories than the N-tosyll and N-(carbobenzoxyl)-protected analogues.
the N-benzyl-protected cyanomethy esters of amino acid analogues are a promising new group of agents for the treatment of neoplastic diseases and inflammatory conditions.
the cyanomethyl esterase series possesses antineoplastic activity, immunosuppressive properties, and the ability to inhibit inflammatory pain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-protective moiety is a key factor in determining the activity of these compounds.
the N-benzyl-protected cyanomethylesters of amino acids are a novel class of antitumor and anti-inflammatory agents.
the N-benzyl group is a good N-protecting group to use in this class of compounds.
